{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-24, raising it inside the ephemeral-store idea: *"may have to make safeguards to ensure that the reflow2 graph is exported at the conclusion of each session"*. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN QUESTION rather than a clause of `dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth` — read in full and judged distinct: that one asks WHAT the enduring artifact is; this asks WHAT MAKES IT RELIABLE. They are answered by different work — one is a storage-model decision, the other is a durability mechanism — and this half is worth something even if the inversion is never taken, because **the export is ALREADY the only copy that survives losing the graph directory.** `loop_status` says exactly that on every call today.

⭐ THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS SHARP. Today an unexported session loses THE SESSION'S WORK and the store still holds the design. Under the inversion, an unexported session loses THE DESIGN. **The same failure changes from an annoyance into data loss, and nothing about the mechanism changes with it.** That is why he flagged it in the same breath as the idea rather than afterwards.

🛑 IT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED, WHICH TAKES THIS OUT OF THE HYPOTHETICAL. `fact:defect-the-export-was-skipped-because-the-instructions-imply-a-stop-that-is-not-needed` (2026-08-15) records an export that was skipped, for a reason nobody would have predicted: the written instructions implied a stop that was not needed. Not negligence — a correct-looking reading of a correct-looking procedure.

EVERY MECHANISM REFLOW2 HAS TODAY IS A NUDGE, AND A NUDGE IS NOT A GUARANTEE:
- The **Stop hook** (`loop_nudge.py`) blocks a finish with unchecked writes — **ONCE**, by its own design, and never twice.
- `loop_status` REPORTS unexported nodes. Reporting is not writing.
- ⚠️ **And the hook is one-harness-only.** `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only` is ACCEPTED: the mechanism is `.claude/settings.json`. A durability guarantee that exists only inside Claude Code is not a durability guarantee — and flo2's users would not be in Claude Code at all.

⇒ **THE GUARANTEE CANNOT LIVE IN THE HARNESS, BECAUSE THE HARNESS IS THE THING THAT MIGHT NOT COME BACK.** A session ends by crashing, by a killed terminal, by a closed laptop, by a container being reaped. None of those run a Stop hook. Anything depending on an orderly shutdown answers a different question from the one that matters.

ROADS, none chosen, listed so the ones not taken keep their reasoning:
1. **EXPORT ON EVERY WRITE (write-through).** Strongest guarantee, and the hosted-tier node already recorded the objection: *"the export being whole-document is correct for an archival action and fatal on a per-change path"*. Dead unless the export becomes incremental.
2. **PERIODIC / DEBOUNCED EXPORT.** Bounded loss instead of no loss. Cheap, harness-independent, and it turns "did the session export?" into "how much did we lose?" — a question with a knob on it.
3. **THE SERVER OWNS IT, NOT THE SESSION.** The shared server already outlives any one session and already knows when a design goes idle; eviction and export become the same event. ⭐ This is the road that fits what already exists — the server is the only component that observes a session ENDING without being the session.
4. **DECLINE THE INVERSION** — the store stays authoritative, the export stays archival. Costs nothing, keeps the 9x inflation and the open-instance ceiling.
5. **A WAL/JOURNAL BESIDE THE BLOB**, replayed on hydrate. Ordinary database engineering, and it re-implements part of what RocksDB already does — named here so nobody proposes it as though it were new.

⚠️ AN OBJECTION TO THE WHOLE FRAME, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down: **RocksDB already solves durability, and solves it well.** Moving the durable copy to a JSON document chooses a weaker durability story on purpose, in exchange for cheap hydration and cheap eviction. That trade may be right for a hosted tier; it is not obviously right for one person on one laptop, where the store has never lost anything.

RECORDED AS A QUESTION, NOT A CONCLUSION.","name":"OPEN — if reflow2.json becomes the enduring artifact, what GUARANTEES it is written?
